title: Make the HTML parser's scripting flag not depend on "scripting was enabled"
body:
https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#other-parsing-state-flags says

> The scripting flag is set to "enabled" if [scripting was enabled](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-n-script) for the [Document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#document) with which the parser is associated when the parser was created, and "disabled" otherwise.

This flag affects parsing of `noscript`, and "scripting was enabled" is disabled for an `<iframe sandbox>` document (without `allow-scripts`) as well as [these](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#script-processing-model:concept-n-noscript):

> scripts in [XMLHttpRequest](https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#xmlhttprequest)'s [responseXML](https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-xmlhttprequest-responsexml) documents, scripts in [DOMParser](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#domparser)-created documents, scripts in documents created by [XSLTProcessor](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#xsltprocessor)'s [transformToDocument](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-xsltprocessor-transformtodocument) feature, and scripts that are first inserted by a script into a [Document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#document) that was created using the [createDocument()](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-domimplementation-createdocument) API.

It's also disabled for `<template>`'s template contents owner document, at least as implemented in WebKit and Chromium (but Gecko parses with scripting flag enabled), see http://software.hixie.ch/utilities/js/live-dom-viewer/saved/11796

This has caused mutation XSS issues in the past, see https://www.acunetix.com/blog/web-security-zone/mutation-xss-in-google-search/

I think it's not great that `noscript` is parsed differently for different documents that can be accessed from script. `noscript` was intended to show content to users when they had scripting disabled *in the browser*. Introducing parsing differences in different places invites XSS bugs.

Would it be web compatible to make the HTML parser's scripting flag only depend on whether the user has disabled scripting?

Alternatively, drop the scripting flag completely and always parse as if scripting is enabled, but this might regress the UX for users who disable script.

@whatwg/html-parser @whatwg/security
